proposal_crosswalk.note: Thirty bills and resolutions in four sessions. Every state-level design - constitutional amendments (direct caps of 2-6 terms, or authorizing the General Assembly to set limits by law) and straight statutes - died in its first Judiciary committee with no recorded vote. The only term-limits measure that passed anything targets Congress, not the State House: H3008, the Article V application for a congressional term limits convention, adopted by the House in March 2025 and the Senate in May 2025 (29-14). The broader Convention of the States application (which includes federal term limits) failed at the last step twice (S133 in 2022, H3676 in 2024) before splitting into single-subject applications that passed in 2025-26.
proposal_crosswalk.proposal_title: Term limits / rotation rules for elected officials

proposal_crosswalk.note: The lane citizens asked about - limiting money - exists mostly as disclosure bills: dark-money ad disclosure (filed by Senate leadership three times), contributor employer disclosure, bank-statement filing, and a corporate-contribution ban. One bill in eight years got a floor vote: H4561 (campaign funds for dependent care) passed the House 53-45 in 2024 and died in Senate Judiciary. Note the direction of the contribution-limit bills actually filed: all five would raise South Carolina's limits, not lower them. No bill proposes lowering a limit; one (H3522) proposed public financing, for Attorney General races only.
proposal_crosswalk.proposal_title: Limits on money in politics / campaign finance reform

proposal_crosswalk.note: Both directions have been filed and neither has ever had a hearing: three bills to allow ranked choice (instant runoff) voting in municipal/local elections (2022, 2023, 2025) and two bills to ban ranked choice voting statewide (2024, 2025). All five died in House Judiciary without a vote. The adjacent runoff-abolition bills (plurality primaries) also never moved.

Twenty-one commission or criteria bills across the 123rd-125th sessions - independent commissions by constitutional amendment, citizens commissions by statute, and binding-criteria acts - and none ever received a hearing or vote; all died in Judiciary committees. The legislature drew the actual maps (Act 117 and Act 118 of 2021-22) on party-line-shaped votes. In May 2026 a mid-decade congressional redraw (H5683) passed the House 74-37 and was shelved on the Senate floor by a 26-18 vote to continue the bill. No commission bill was filed in the 126th session - the first session without one in this record.

The most movement of any proposal. Enacted: S70, the School Board Ethics Act (Act 191 of 2026, 39-2 and 109-4), after two earlier versions died. Nearly enacted: H3570, the economic-interests disclosure rewrite, passed the House 102-0 and the Senate 40-0 in different versions and died in conference in May 2026 - and a piece of it (naming the government body behind budget-paid income) reappeared as FY 2026-27 budget proviso 117.219. Everything else - tax-return disclosure, e-filing audits, special-purpose-district coverage, ethics-fine ballot bars - died in Senate or House Judiciary without votes.
proposal_crosswalk.proposal_title: Better financial-disclosure and conflict-of-interest tracking (incl. PACs)

proposal_crosswalk.note: A small but real lane with one law: the REACH Act (S38, Act 26 of 2021) requires every public college student to study the founding documents; it passed 45-0 and 91-12 on its second try after the 2019 version passed the Senate and died in a House committee. The K-12 design citizens described - a required middle-school civics unit with hands-on projects (H3547, 2025) - sits in House Education without a vote. Civic-education money has moved through the budget instead: a Clemson civic-engagement center study (FY 2024-25 proviso 45.11) and $2.5 million for a USC civic leadership center (FY 2026-27, in proviso 118.21). No bill proposes a neutral voter-information tool.
proposal_crosswalk.proposal_title: Better voter education / civics and neutral civic information tools

proviso_crosswalk.note: Hand-curated ethics/elections/lobbying/civics provisos from Part IB of each enacted appropriations act (term-matched candidate sets in provisos/{year}/). Budget provisos are one-year rules enacted inside the annual budget bill; votes attach to the whole appropriations bill (or a named amendment), never to one proviso. FY 2020-21 had no enacted Part IB (COVID continuing resolution) - stated explicitly per the workflow's none-found rule.

cycles.gap_note: No enacted Part IB this cycle: H5201 died in committee during COVID; the state ran on continuing resolution H3411 plus CARES acts.

data_limits: The set is keyword-discovered from official full-text search plus a title/summary scan of the certified universe; it is a curated selection, not a proven-complete universe of accountability bills. Four REACH Act civics bills were hand-added from the certified universe because their text contains none of the issue's search terms.
South Carolina publishes committee outcomes in bill histories but never committee vote tallies; no committee vote counts exist anywhere in this record and none may be implied.
Party labels are not attached to sponsors or floor votes in this pack: the roster/ballot join was not fetched for this brief, so the brief makes no party claims.

Floor roll-call counts are verbatim from the chamber vote-history tables; motions to table, to adopt amendments, or to continue are procedural, and only passage/reading/adoption votes are used as support signals. The Senate's 26-18 vote on H5683 was a motion to continue (shelve) the bill, not a vote on passage.

Article V applications and internal rule changes travel as resolutions: concurrent resolutions (H3008, H3007) take effect when both chambers adopt them and never go to the governor; House resolutions (H4692) bind only the House.
For non-enacted 126th-session (2025-2026) bills, disposition is 'did not pass' as of the collection date (2026-08-26), after the regular session's final regular calendar.
FY 2020-21 has no enacted Part IB proviso set (COVID continuing resolution), so budget-proviso coverage runs FY 2021-22 through FY 2026-27.
The six Phase 2 constituent proposals are Forum process input from Community Conversations (labels [P-...]), not verified facts.

bills.theme: Open government: public records and meetings
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Ways and Means)

bills.title: Budget Transparency Act
bills.plain_topic: The Budget Transparency Act: agencies must publish salary detail with their budget requests.
bills.theme: Open government: public records and meetings
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Ways and Means)

bills.title: Term limits
bills.plain_topic: Proposes a constitutional amendment letting the General Assembly set term limits for its own members by ordinary law.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Judiciary)

bills.title: Term Limits
bills.plain_topic: Would cap service by statute: six terms in the House or four terms in the Senate.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Judiciary)

bills.title: Earmark Responsibility, Accountability, Integrity, and Transparency Act
bills.plain_topic: Would require organizations receiving state earmarks to file itemized public accountings, receipts included.
bills.theme: Open government: public records and meetings
bills.sponsors_raw: Reps. Huff, Gilreath, McCabe and Cromer
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Ways and Means)

bills.title: Constitutional Amendment, dual office holding exclusions
bills.plain_topic: Constitutional amendment exempting unpaid positions from the dual-office-holding ban.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Judiciary)

bills.title: Term limits
bills.plain_topic: Would cap total General Assembly service at twelve years by statute, paired with a raise in members' in-district compensation.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Judiciary)

bills.title: Election Transparency and Accountability Act
bills.plain_topic: Election-procedure package: free records, observer rights, equipment chain-of-custody rules.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Judiciary)

bills.title: Reapportionment, Congressional Districts
bills.plain_topic: Would have redrawn South Carolina's congressional districts mid-decade, starting with the 2026 election; died in House Judiciary.
bills.sponsors_raw: Reps. Pace, Edgerton, Kilmartin, White, Cromer and Gilreath
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Judiciary)

bills.title: FOIA fees
bills.plain_topic: Would let legislators get public records free of charge for legislative work.
bills.theme: Open government: public records and meetings
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Judiciary)

bills.title: Term limits for members of General Assembly
bills.plain_topic: Proposes a constitutional amendment capping service at four House terms or two Senate terms.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (House Judiciary)

bills.title: Redistricting, Congressional Districts
bills.plain_topic: The May 2026 mid-decade congressional redraw: passed the House 74-37 after dozens of amendment fights, then the Senate voted 26-18 to shelve it.
bills.sponsors_raw: Reps. Rankin, Pace, C. Mitchell, Cromer, Gilreath, Bustos, Magnuson, Edgerton, Burns, Oremus, Bailey, Guest, Brittain, Chumley, J.E. Johnson, Haddon, Jordan, Lawson, Lowe, McGinnis, B. Newton, W. Newton, G.M. Smith, White, Willis and McCravy
bills.stage: Passed the House 74-37; shelved on the Senate floor by a 26-18 vote to continue

passage_votes.motion: (Redistricting, Congressional Districts) Passage of Bill
(Redistricting, Congressional Districts) Passage of Bill

bills.title: Apply Ethics Laws to Political Party Chairmen
bills.plain_topic: Would apply the state's ethics, campaign-practices, and lobbying laws to political party chairmen.
bills.sponsors_raw: Senators Kimbrell, Davis, Johnson, Verdin, Hembree, Turner, Massey, Rice, Cash, Reichenbach, Leber, Fernandez and Climer
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)

bills.title: Term Limits Constitutional Amendment
bills.plain_topic: Proposes a constitutional amendment capping service at three Senate terms or six House terms.
bills.sponsors_raw: Senators Reichenbach, Fernandez, Rice, Garrett, Chaplin, Elliott, Stubbs, Zell and Climer
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)

bills.title: Freedom of Information
bills.plain_topic: Would give public bodies a five-day deadline to produce records, with silence counting as a denial and a violation.
bills.theme: Open government: public records and meetings
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)

bills.title: Ethics - Local Government Lobbying
bills.plain_topic: Would extend the lobbying law to lobbying of county and city governments and require an online list of registered lobbyists - filed by Senate leadership of both parties.
bills.sponsors_raw: Senators Bennett, Alexander, Peeler, Rankin, Williams, Grooms and Jackson
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)

bills.title: School Board Ethics
bills.plain_topic: The School Board Ethics Act (Act 191 of 2026): a required code of ethics and training for elected school board members - this set's one enacted ethics law.
bills.stage: Became law (Act 191)

passage_votes.motion: (School Board Ethics) 3rd Reading
(School Board Ethics) Passage of Bill

bills.title: Ethics Fines
bills.plain_topic: Would keep candidates off the ballot unless they declare ethics fines owed and enroll in a payment plan.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)

bills.title: Campaign Contributor Information
bills.plain_topic: Would require campaign reports to list the occupation and employer of anyone giving more than $100 - filed by Senate leadership of both parties.
bills.sponsors_raw: Senators Bennett, Peeler, Jackson, Rankin, Grooms, Sabb, Williams and Alexander
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)

bills.title: Interest on Campaign Bank Accounts
bills.plain_topic: Would pool interest earned on campaign bank accounts (plus 1% of deposits) to fund State Ethics Commission enforcement.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)

bills.title: Campaign Bank Account Statements
bills.plain_topic: Would require candidates to file their actual campaign bank statements alongside each quarterly campaign report.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)

bills.title: Ballot Initiative
bills.plain_topic: Proposes a constitutional amendment creating a ballot-initiative process for enacting or repealing laws.
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)

bills.title: Campaign Practices
bills.plain_topic: Would require independent expenditure committees to disclose who is behind their election ads.
bills.sponsors_raw: Senators Bennett, Hembree, Rankin, Turner, Massey and Campsen
bills.stage: Died in its first committee (Senate Judiciary)
